title: TI P4-08: one-off content copy tool (old backend to new) and dry run
description:
## Goal
A one-off, idempotent tool that copies Threat Intelligence's published content and media from the OLD backend to the NEW backend, with a dry run. No generic backend-to-backend copy command exists in Papyrus; this ticket builds the smallest one for this migration.

## Context (FACT)
- `papyrus ops content` on develop has: inspect, schema-check, list, import-markus (Git Markus files to CMS), export-published (CMS to a Markus build directory; article and page types only), convert-bodies (legacy body[] to bodyMarkus and bodyIr, Item and PublishedItem only), markus-derive, publish, unpublish, rebuild, upload-preview, backfill-item-body-attachments, scrub-item-inline-body. None copies between two backends, and import-markus/export-published are the Markus path: a round trip through them would drop Pretext-only fields (section, deck, dateline, byline, pullQuotes, editorial.customExcerpt, layout, editionDate).
- Old PublishedItem rows hold the legacy inline body as a string list (18 rows) and pullQuotes; Papyrus develop's schema keeps body and adds bodyMarkus, bodyIr, aliases, metadata, so legacy rows are valid there and convert-bodies upgrades them (P4-09).
- The old AppSync API accepts IAM (SigV4) calls, so the admin SSO session can read it; the new backend is written through the authoring client (SigV4 as the site's authoring role <siteId>-papyrus-authoring or the admin role).
- Models to copy (counts): Edition 1, PublishedEdition 1, EditionItem 18, PublishedEditionItem 18, Item 20 (18 published + 2 private editorial-doctrine items), PublishedItem 18, MediaAsset 24, PublishedMediaAsset 24, NewsroomSection 6, Tag 8, ItemTag 24. S3: media/ prefix 65 objects, 160 MB (storage keys are referenced by the media rows, keep keys identical in the new bucket).
- Not copied by default: assignments, messages, procedure rows, references and the knowledge graph (research data), corpora/ and newsroom/ prefixes in S3 (open question Q4). The old backend is retained until the retire ticket, so nothing is lost by leaving them.
- DB is authoritative: 6 articles differ from the Git seed (see P4-01); the copy reads the live DB.
- The tool is TI-specific and one-off: keep it in the TI repo under procedures/ or scripts/ with a header stating it is deleted after the migration (YAGNI: no Papyrus API surface); decide at implementation whether it needs a Papyrus helper (then PR to develop).

## Exact steps
1. Gherkin: "a dry run reports per-model created/updated/unchanged counts and writes nothing"; "applying twice is a no-op the second time"; "ids, slugs, versionNumber, publishedAt and S3 keys are preserved".
2. Implement read (old API via SigV4, paginated) and write (new API via the authoring client), in dependency order: NewsroomSection, Tag, Edition, Item, MediaAsset, EditionItem, ItemTag, then Published* models, then S3 media objects (same key, same content type, copy by aws s3 cp between buckets; verify ETag/size).
3. --dry-run prints a table; --apply writes; both emit JSON with counts and skipped reasons.
4. Run the dry run against the new backend (from P4-06) and review the output with Ryan.

## Acceptance checks
- Dry run: exact counts per model equal the FACT list; zero errors; zero writes (new API row counts unchanged, S3 object count unchanged).
- Tool tests green (fixture-based, no AWS).

## Rollback
Nothing written in this ticket (dry run only).

## Risks
The new schema's required fields or enum values may reject old rows (typeStatus, sectionStatus, layout JSON): the dry run must validate each row against the new schema and list failures. Large mp4 copy time (two 26 MB videos).

## Needs Ryan
Review of the dry-run table. No AWS writes in this ticket.

## Common rules (Phase 4 Threat Intelligence)
- Plan and facts: the assessment comment on the Phase 4 ticket (PPY-332889). Pattern: docs/migrations/pilobol-us.md and docs/standard-site.md 3.2 on origin/develop.
- Ryan: Threat Intelligence is PRE-PRODUCTION; goal is to dogfood the new backend CMS UX before converting anth.us (production). Treat as a hard cutover with brief downtime accepted unless Ryan says otherwise (open question Q1). The OLD app d3on1y5vlrxmam and its backend stay untouched and serving until the retire ticket.
- Read AGENTS.local.md first. AWS_PROFILE=legacy, us-east-1 (SSO is Ryan's). Never print env var or secret VALUES (names only). Never run ampx pipeline-deploy locally. Creating, changing or deleting AWS resources needs Ryan's explicit yes in chat for that step; deleting data or stacks is done by Ryan or on his explicit yes. Read-only AWS calls are fine.
- NEVER use /Users/home/Projects/Pilobol.us as a build dir. TI repo work: fresh clone under /Users/home/Projects/ (delete afterwards), feature branch + PR, never push to its main. Papyrus repo: worktree of origin/develop under /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus-worktrees/, branch feature/PPY-<id>-<slug>, PR into develop, never merge to main, never git stash, trailer Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>, PR body ends with the Claude Code generated-with line. In /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus (the board checkout) only run kbs; never git add or commit there.
- Gherkin first for any Papyrus behavior change (AGENTS.md). Long clear names, no line-level comments.
- Update this ticket with branch, PR link and command output when done.
